articles.title: How Sky Studios Elstree Built for the Future
articles.summary: Managing director Noel Tovey on starting a lot from scratch with sustainability, accessibility, training and community at its core — and opening its stages to the entire industry.
articles.content:
Sky Studios Elstree, while in its infancy, has put down roots to outlast all of its peers.

Opened in 2022, this 27.5-acre studio in Borehamwood, Hertfordshire, has 12 sound stages ranging from 10,000 to 40,000 square feet, a six-acre backlot and sprawling production offices, workshops, prop stores and dressing facilities. Since cutting the red ribbon, the Comcast-owned production behemoth has welcomed over 50 productions, including more than 20 major feature films — both Wicked movies and Jurassic World Rebirth among them — as well as high-end TV shows and commercials. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-article-mid-article-uid0' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article1","mid-articleX","mid","mid-article"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article") .addSize([[300,250],[2,2],[300,251],[620,350],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4],[300,251]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; }); Related Stories Lifestyle John Malkovich Sets West End Return With Rosalind Eleazar in 'History' Movies We Now Know What Robert Pattinson Was Doing When the James Bond Casting News Broke

But even while the studio's slate of star-spangled projects continues to grow and its reputation for large-scale innovation is steadily nurtured — you might be shocked to learn Jonathan Bailey's attempt to collect dinosaur DNA wasn't actually shot on a cliff edge on a remote island in the Atlantic Ocean — the team here prides itself most on what audiences don't see. Built around four key pillars of sustainability, accessibility, training and community, getting up to speed on Sky Studios Elstree (not to be confused with the nearby, entirely separate Elstree Studios) is not unlike stepping into the future: This is a studio that has harnessed the power of a post-pandemic birth to meticulously design and construct a lot that will continue to thrive for decades, if not centuries, from now.

“Building a studio from scratch meant that we could take advantage of all the technologies that we could see coming,” begins Noel Tovey, managing director at Sky Studios Elstree. “On paper [and] from the start, it was going to be the most sustainable studio facility we can possibly build.” blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-dsk-tab-mid-article2-uid1' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid","mid-article2","mid-articleX"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article2") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,350],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

The studio deftly straddles the intimacy of community-led initiatives and craft-training programs with impressively lofty standards for environment-focused targets. They have 140,000 square feet of rooftop solar panels that help reduce carbon emissions by up to 500 tonnes annually, boast 80 electric vehicle charging points around the site, harvest rainwater and remain committed to zero landfill-bound waste. A hydrogen hybrid generator was trialled on the backlot before being used on two Sky productions, including Danny Dyer's Mr Bigstuff , and Sky Entertainment Group scripted productions now budget for a sustainable innovation trial, which encourages teams to test new approaches to reduce their environmental impact.

Tovey isn't here just to talk about his team's axing of single-use packaging or championing of local biodiversity through the introduction of on-site beehives, but the expansive work through which Sky Studio Elstree remains steadfast in cultivating the next generation of film and TV talent. More than 18,500 young people have visited the Sky Up Academy Studios at the Elstree base since 2024; one of their annual programs hosts eight paid trainees, while a three-day in-person work experience scheme offers 60 young people in the Hertfordshire area an opportunity to discover the magic of industry roles once a year. The studio has also developed purpose-built accessibility with a dedicated Accessibility Committee, step-free access on site, dropped kerbs, braille signage and lift access to all upper floors in an attempt to set an industry-wide benchmark. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-thr-article-mid-articleX-uid2' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["btf","mid-articleX","mid"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-articleX") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,350],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4]]) .setLazyLoadMultiplier(2) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

Below, Tovey dives into those aforementioned pillars and talks about welcoming the entire industry — not just their own commissions — to Sky Studios Elstree. From Amazon Prime Video's Last One Laughing and Masters of the Universe , A24's Elden Ring or Warner Bros.' Wuthering Heights , the success here isn't just raising the bar for rivals, but letting everyone take a share of the (sustainably made) pie.

Sky Studios Elstree is not just a studio for Sky projects, is it?

No, so primarily, we were built as a facility to [accommodate for] in-house production. Sky have got a big slate. As do our partners at NBCUniversal and all the companies that they own or have a financial stake in. And I think it was felt — and this was before I joined Sky, so I'm surmising the discussions here — but I think it was felt that because of the boom in production activity [and] the advent of the streamers coming to London in a big way, the Netflixes and Amazons and what have you, all the existing studios and stage space got swallowed up very quickly. Universal have always made features in the U.K., and they've got a long history of [that]… [But] there was a need for stage space that could be focused on homegrown production for Sky and also then production coming in from the U.S., and they thought, “Well, we've got a blank sheet of paper. What shall we build?”

This is when sustainability became high on the agenda. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-thr-article-mid-articleX-uid3' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["btf","mid-articleX","mid"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-articleX") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,350],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4]]) .setLazyLoadMultiplier(2) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

It gave us the opportunity to look at construction methods [and] look at trying to be as light [as possible] on carbon use. For example, the concrete use in the stages here is minimal, and where we do use it, it's as low-carbon as possible. And then, thinking afresh, we knew that we were going to put solar panels on the roof, so you build the roof structure to be able to take that [with] all air source heat pumps. We don't have any fossil fuels piped into the lot. We know that productions use generators from time to time. How can we make life easy for them? Well, there are two ways. Universal Production Services, our partner here at the studios who supply the lighting and rigging, they've spec-ed their generators to be as green as possible using biofuel, and also now they're investing in battery technology. So you have a hybrid generator.

Building a studio from scratch meant that we could take advantage of all the technologies that we could see coming, and also make the site easy for productions to use. And from my experience, productions, by the time they get to us, they have a schedule. Once they arrive, they've got a delivery date. They're working back from that. So they don't have time to start thinking about all these extra sustainability things, really, unless they're a big budget move and they have a sustainability person on board from the start. So we can cater to broad ranges of production budgets. We'll try and do the heavy lifting ourselves. We'll manage their waste. We'll find a company like Olio that can look after all the excess catering food. We've got a ton of biofuel on the lot, so it's easier for people to purchase it from us than to go off-site, and also we sell it cheaper than you can buy it commercially. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-thr-article-mid-articleX-uid4' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["btf","mid-articleX","mid"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-articleX") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,350],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4]]) .setLazyLoadMultiplier(2) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

What is that commitment to sustainability rooted in, in the context of the ethos at Sky?

On paper [and] from the start, it was going to be the most sustainable studio facility we can possibly build. It was designed from the ground up. We've got 140,000 square feet of solar panels on the roofs, for example. We envisaged quite a lot of crew may have electric vehicles, so we over-delivered car charging in their multi-storey car park. We probably got more than we need, but we were building for the future. For example, all the buildings and stages are super-insulated, which does well for sound insulation, but also heat retention, or in the summer, cooling retention.

Do you get good feedback from the talent about the sustainability features in place?

The talent, I don't know how much they know [about what] we're doing. ( Laughs .) But certainly from the productions, and also when a production has to submit their sustainability card to [BAFTA Albert Studio Sustainability Standard], for example, you've already got an Albert scorecard for the studio at 95 percent just by being here. You tick a few of their scorecard boxes, and then we handle the waste management. Zero waste is going to landfill from us. Everything that can be recycled is recycled, so it's very easy to track. We can give data and reports of that waste journey.

And is this quite novel compared to other studios in the area?

Yeah. I think that actually, there's a lot of activity now in this area. And because somewhere like Pinewood — [where] Disney shoot a lot of their productions, their Marvel and Lucasfilm, etc. — they have a big in-house team at Disney that are [now] looking at this. So actually, Pinewood, even though they haven't got the solar panels that we've got, sustainable fuels and waste management, all those sorts of things, they do a pretty good job of. The same with Warner Bros. at Leavesden — or Skydance, as it is now. They're all looking at doing that, and I think it's good. I think as an industry together, we're all moving in that direction. We're all trying to make productions' life easy, so they don't have to think about it too hard. They can just step into the studio and get on with making the film or TV shows, and we do the heavy lifting. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-thr-article-mid-articleX-uid5' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["btf","mid-articleX","mid"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-articleX") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,350],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4]]) .setLazyLoadMultiplier(2) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

Could you talk a little bit about the projects that you attract?

We've got some very large sound stages. Because they're so large, you need a certain size of production that requires them, and that tends to be set-built [projects]. [With] Wicked , that was obviously an imaginary land. They did go to shoot some locations, like the fields in Norfolk with the tulips and what have you, but the rest of it was thought up in the directors' and production designers' minds. So you need a huge, voluminous soundstage in which to create these sets, and we've got those. That, by default, [is] the type of [productions] that tend to come to Sky Studios Elstree. We did the last Jurassic [ Jurassic World Rebirth ] here. We've got quite a large back lot, and any shows that need a good back lot set… So Paddington shot here, and they had quite a big element of water work, so they built some boats on gimbals. I hope I'm not giving away the secrets behind the cameras. ( Laughs .) But they'll shoot some of the stuff on location, then they'll come and do the really technical, difficult bit back with us, where you can control the environment 100 percent. I don't know if you've seen the last Jurassic , but they build that huge cliff on the back lot — where they've got to take the DNA from the pterodactyl egg.

And it amused me that people walking past the studio had no idea that you Jonathan Bailey and Co. were just out on the backlot dangling from ropes. Well, slightly more than that. ( Laughs .) Lots of safety harnesses involved. […] So because you've got to manufacture all of this stuff, you need huge workspaces. You need workshops. We've got plaster shops and carpentry shops and 3D printing areas and costume design spaces and costume breakdown. Then you've got big crowd scenes. You need to change all the crowd, get them through hair and makeup. Then you need to all go for lunch somewhere that's big enough to cater for them and the crew. And if you think we're doing two or three of these [projects] at any given time, that's quite a lot of space that all these productions need. […] And I must say that I've seen a move since Wicked [where] directors want to create things in camera and not to rely too much on visual effects in post. So a lot of this stuff is made and built for real, and there's lots of complex special effects rigs and clever set design to make sure that they can shoot some of this stuff for real. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-thr-article-mid-articleX-uid6' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["btf","mid-articleX","mid"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-articleX") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,350],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4]]) .setLazyLoadMultiplier(2) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

I also wanted to ask about the talent programmes you have, and how Sky Studios Elstree is trying to cultivate the next generation of film and TV craftspeople.

We're doing a lot. Sky, before they devised this studio, had a long-running program at Sky Osterley called Sky Up, and it was designed for school children to be able to peek behind the camera on presenting, sports, news, all sorts of things that Sky did. Then when this studio was devised, it became apparent that there was a way in for us to do a bit more about the creative side of filmmaking and TV dram. We were lucky to have all the learnings and all the infrastructure that Sky had from Sky Up in their center. So [now] we have a Sky Up Academy here, and school children come along. We do a classroom in the morning, a classroom in the afternoon. Prior to arriving here, they've been sent a pack to their school, and they work through the different projects that they can do. And and ultimately, they come here and they make a little short movie in a little XR studio that we've got, and as part of that, they learn about all the jobs behind the camera.

[With] local college Elstree Screen Arts […] we're focusing a lot more on the technical crew. There is a shortage in the U.K. of the crafts, so we decided to support that [side] of the industry. There are plasterers, carpenters, the on-set electricians, scenic painters. And just to digress for a moment, there was a thought that virtual production was going to be huge and nobody will need scenic backings anymore. Well, most of the stages here right now, all their backings are scenic-painted, which is fantastic to see. Over the years, they became green and blue, and then virtual, and now they're going back to scenic, and it's a dying art. So in order to get people interested in it, we thought, ‘Well, let's have this talent and education stuff happening here, right in the heart of the studio.' And it's there. It's there on all the stages. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-thr-article-mid-articleX-uid7' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["btf","mid-articleX","mid"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-articleX") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,350],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4]]) .setLazyLoadMultiplier(2) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

Why do you owe that return to practical effects to?

My personal view is visual effects have become so good and so easy to access for a lot of filmmakers and TV makers that the audiences have been oversaturated with them. So, doing it for real, I think you can tell as a viewer, particularly on the big screen, when something's real and something is added afterwards, perhaps… In Wicked , we had the enchanted forest with the Yellow Brick Road going through it, and they planted it up. We had grow lights on the stage keeping plants alive. It was full of earth and turf, and it smelt like a forest. So that must add something for a performance, surely.

I know there's a big emphasis on community for Sky Studios Elstree as well, and working with local authorities to welcome the surrounding area in.

We've got quite a small team here, but we love getting involved with the local community, and during the strikes a few years ago, we had some empty stages. Our new productions weren't going to fill them. So we put a cinema on the stages, and we invited all the parents and their kids. We filled the stage with bean bags and a big screen at the end and we got some popcorn and hot dog stands. We invited the local community. And just to see the young children's faces walking into a studio. […] There's a YMCA community center for young families, and their garden fell into disrepair during COVID, and we twisted productions' arms and they gave us some timber, and we got some skips from our waste company, and a whole bunch of the staff went down there, security and cleaning, gardeners… And last week we opened a fully refurbished, brand-new garden for the YMCA. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-thr-article-mid-articleX-uid8' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["btf","mid-articleX","mid"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-articleX") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,350],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4]]) .setLazyLoadMultiplier(2) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

Aged seven years old, I was lucky enough to visit both Pinewood and Shepperton. I lived quite near, and seeing that these major Hollywood movies were actually shot in London and not in L.A., I didn't believe it. It's great for the local community, particularly the filmic history that this area has. I'm sat in this meeting room, and I can see a building across the road that we lease as workshop space. That used to be MGM Studios. That's where Stanley Kubrick shot. And just knowing that it was there and the film history just makes me feel great about coming to work every day.

Is it fair to say to Sky Studios Elstree is the first of its kind in lots of ways?

I think it probably is. Knowing a bit about some of the more recent additions to the likes of Pinewood and Shepperton, and also Leavesden, they've also done very similar things to Sky. But we've built the whole studio with all the sustainability and accessibility in mind, and it wasn't an afterthought. It was designed that way from the beginning. That's a big differentiator here.

articles.content:
Brad Pitt was enthusiastic last night on The Further Mis-Adventures Of Cliff Booth when he was asked about Amazon MGM confirming Robert Pattinson as the next James Bond .

"I love this idea," Pitt said. "I love what he's been doing. I love his choices, and I think he's the real deal. That's great. Good call."

Pitt was then asked by a reporter whether he would ever star as a villain in a Bond film. He was game.

"You know, I'd like to do that," he said. "My man Javier [Bardem] did it so well. It's tall shoes, but I'd take that on." Related Stories News Robert Pattinson As James Bond? Baz Bamigboye Has Some Thoughts News Robert Pattinson As Bond Or Bond Villain: What Did The Actor Say Years Ago?

Pattinson was unveiled as the next Bond yesterday. The British actor described the gig as a "dream come true" in a statement after the news was announced. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-dsk-tab-mid-article1-uid0' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article1","mid","mid-articleX","mid-article","300x251"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article") .addSize([[2,2],[300,250],[620,350],[300,251],[501,282],[3,3],[2,4],[4,2],[620,366]]) .exemptFromSleep() .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; }); Watch on Deadline if ( !window.pmc.harmony?.isEventAdScheduledTime() ) { pmcCnx.cmd.push(function() { pmcCnx({ settings: { plugins: { pmcAtlasMG: { iabPlcmt: 2, } } }, playerId: '32fe25c4-79aa-406a-af44-69b41e969e71', playlistId: '0199e506-e642-7728-8264-463efe71337b', }).render("connatix_contextual_player_div"); }); } else { // This should only be get called when page cache is not cleared and it's event time. window.pmc.harmony?.switchToHarmonyPlayer(); }

articles.content:
Indian actress, director and social advocate Nandita Das and Syrian star Taim Hassan are set to be honored by the Doha Film Festival with Creative Excellence Awards during the event's opening ceremony on Thursday.

Das has acted in more than 40 feature films, starting with Deepa Mehta's “Fire,” which depicts a relationship between two women in an Indian household. She's subsequently worked with top Indian directors such as Mrinal Sen, Shyam Benegal, Adoor Gopalakrishnan, Rituporno Ghosh and Mani Ratnam. Her directorial debut “Firaaq” — about the aftermath of the 2002 sectarian carnage in Gujarat, where 3,000 Muslims were killed — played at Toronto in 2008 and went on to travel widely and score many awards. She's been a member of the main jury at Cannes Film Festival twice, in 2005 and 2013. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-variety-article-mid-article-uid0' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article1","mid-articleX","mid","mid-article"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article") .addSize([[300,250],[2,2],[300,251],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; }); Related Stories Hollywood's Next Big Deal: Will Netflix Make an M&A Play for NBCU? 'Nobody Wants This' Renewed for Season 4 at Netflix

Hassan made his breakthrough playing young ruler Fatimid Caliph Al-Adid in Syrian director Hatem Ali's historical epics “Al-Zir Salem” (2000) and “Saladin” (2001). He has led all five seasons of hit Arabic TV show "Al Hayba," about a family of arms smugglers working the border between Syria and Lebanon, a role that has made him a household name across the region and reached international audiences on Netflix. Hassan's more recent work includes the show “Taj” (2024), in which he plays a boxer resisting the French occupation of Syria; hit political drama “Under the Seventh Ground” (2025); and thriller series “Mawlana” (2026).

"Cinema transcends borders, challenges perceptions and brings us closer to our shared humanity. Nandita Das and Taim Hassan represent the very best of this power,” said Doha Film Institute CEO Fatma Hassan Alremaihi, who also heads the festival. “Their remarkable artistry, courage of expression and unwavering commitment to authentic storytelling resonates far beyond geographical and cultural boundaries.” blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-dsk-tab-mid-article2-uid1' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid","mid-article2","mid-articleX"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article2") .addSize([[320,480],[300,250],[300,251],[2,4],[4,2],[620,366],[300,450]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

articles.title: John Malkovich Sets West End Return With Rosalind Eleazar in 'History'
articles.summary: The production is the West End debut of playwright Rebecca Reid.
articles.content:
John Malkovich is returning to the West End for the first time in 30 years.

Hot on the heels of immense Oscar buzz for his latest outing in Martin McDonagh's festival favorite Wild Horse Nine , the Oscar nominee will co-star with Rosalind Eleazar in a production of Rebecca Reid's History .

The play is set to mark Reid's West End debut, and will have a limited run at Wyndham's Theatre from May 17 to Aug. 7 2027. It follows Wren, who once had a vibrant, creative life until motherhood, sleepless nights and doomscrolling took over. On a reckless whim, she invites James — the ex who once defined her — to lunch. Their reunion forces Wren to reconsider a relationship she believed belonged firmly in the past. As the conversation unfolds, she discovers that the story she thought was finished may still be taking shape. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-article-mid-article-uid0' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article1","mid-articleX","mid","mid-article"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article") .addSize([[300,250],[2,2],[300,251],[620,350],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4],[300,251]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; }); Related Stories Movies We Now Know What Robert Pattinson Was Doing When the James Bond Casting News Broke News Over 400 U.K. Industry Figures Demand End to "Culture of Open Secrets" After Russell Brand Trial

“I couldn't be more delighted to start work in the months to come on this fascinating new play, opposite Rosalind Eleazar and directed by Matthew Dunster,” Malkovich said this week about coming back to the London stage. “I can't wait. Rebecca Reid has written something rare — a play that is complex and profoundly human.”

Malkovich has wowed audiences this year as a terminally ill CIA operative in the buddy-comedy Wild Horse Nine opposite Sam Rockwell. He's also known for roles in Being John Malkovich , Dangerous Liaisons , and In the Line of Fire .

Eleazar, meanwhile, is a British star who most recently led Chris Rock's Misty Green . She has a supporting role in Apple TV's hit series Slow Horses and was the face of Netflix's Harlan Coben adaptation Missing You .

articles.content:
Catherine Zeta-Jones vehicle Kill Jackie was instrumental in Fremantle posting third quarter revenue up nearly 8%.

The action series, in which Zeta Jones plays an art dealer with a dark past, was singled out for driving Q3 sales to €482M ($530.4M), up 7.8% on €447M for the same three months in 2025.

The series – from Fremantle, Steel String Pictures and Amazon MGM Studios, landed at HBO Max over the summer, following on from major distribution agreements with AMC+ and Prime Video.

Also flagged were a Prime Video deal for the Baywatch reboot and other new launches such as Netflix's unscripted series Wonka's The Golden Ticket and drama series Minerva Academy , which topped Top 10 charts in 62 territories. Good thing the regenerated Doctor Who just took another step forward then with around half a dozen UK production houses informed over the past week they have made the tender shortlist. One will produce the next edition of the iconic sci-fi series from 2028.

Deadline understands that Jed Mercurio ‘s bid with Hat Trick founder Jimmy Mulville has made the shortlist via their Hat Trick Mercurio indie. Others we believe have made it through are Line of Duty producer World Productions and Criminal Record maker STV Studios . articles.title: India's Music Economy Hits $1.8 Billion as Independent Music Claims 43% of Streams, EY Report Finds
articles.summary: Music generated an estimated INR17,400 crore ($1.8 billion) worth of economic activity in India in 2025, 45% more than two years earlier, according to a new EY study backed by the Indian Performing Right Society (IPRS). Digital platforms accounted for 52% of that value. Combined label and publishing revenue hit a record INR5,433 crore ($563 […]
articles.content:
Music generated an estimated INR17,400 crore ($1.8 billion) worth of economic activity in India in 2025, 45% more than two years earlier, according to a new EY study backed by the Indian Performing Right Society ( IPRS ).

Digital platforms accounted for 52% of that value. Combined label and publishing revenue hit a record INR5,433 crore ($563 million) in 2025, up from INR4,938 crore ($512 million) in 2023. Publishing and performance income rose 79% over the same stretch, climbing from INR628 crore ($65 million) to INR1,125 crore ($117 million). blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-variety-article-mid-article-uid0' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article1","mid-articleX","mid","mid-article"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article") .addSize([[300,250],[2,2],[300,251],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; }); Related Stories Jimmy Fallon Works on Big Plays for NBC's 'Tonight': 'Fockers' After Football, L.A. Olympics, 75th Show Anniversary in 2029 (EXCLUSIVE) Mariska Hargitay, Steve Carell and Jimmy Fallon Among Stars Set for NBC's 100th Anniversary Special

Indians streamed close to six trillion tracks last year. Independent artists took 43% of digital listening, compared with under 35% in 2023, a shift the report ties to rising appetite for regional-language and artist-driven music.

The report, titled “It Is a Good Time to Be in Music: India's Music Creator Economy Report Vol. 2,” also found that jobs in the organized segment rose 50% to between 60,000 and 70,000. Annual output of original songs climbed to between 22,000 and 27,000. Live is growing too: India staged more than 130 days of concerts in 2025 that each drew over 10,000 people, double the 65 recorded in 2023.

Scale has yet to translate into global clout. India slipped one place to 15th in IFPI's recorded music revenue rankings and sits 23rd for music collections under CISAC. Music revenue per head was $0.40, against $44.70 in the U.S. Of the 233 million Indians who streamed music in 2025, only 14 million to 16 million paid for a subscription.

A survey of more than 5,900 JioSaavn users, conducted with the streamer and focused on Gen Z habits, showed music running through the day. Some 88% listen for at least an hour daily. Travel (85%), relaxing (76%) and work (56%) topped the list of listening occasions, with studying also featuring strongly. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-dsk-tab-mid-article2-uid1' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid","mid-article2","mid-articleX"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article2") .addSize([[320,480],[300,250],[300,251],[2,4],[4,2],[620,366],[300,450]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

Creators are conflicted. While 75% believe there are more opportunities than before, 76% say those openings are getting harder to exploit. More platforms, direct reach and overseas audiences have arrived alongside unpredictable income, a fight for discoverability, complicated rights administration, higher marketing spend and new risks from AI.

Lyricist and screenwriter Javed Akhtar , speaking at the launch, said the figures left him “very depressed.” Of the roughly INR5,000 crore ($518 million) that reaches the production side, he estimated that composers, lyricists and singers receive less than INR1,000 crore ($104 million). “So something is seriously wrong even today. Seriously wrong,” he said.

The report puts licensing compliance among eligible businesses at around 4%, the same figure Akhtar cited for hotels, restaurants, bars and events. He said he had proposed to the IPRS board that the government add a question on royalty payments to the GST (goods and services tax) form. “So, it's only lack of intention. Lack of intention,” Akhtar said.

“Could you imagine that someday you would need to patent the voices?” Akhtar asked, adding that the family of the late singer Kishore Kumar receives nothing from the many songs now made in the singer's voice, and calling for new international rules to deal with AI.

“India's music economy is creating significant value, but its long-term success will be measured by how effectively that value reaches creators. Strengthening monetization avenues, rights management and export capabilities through creator education can help translate rising consumption into sustainable growth for the entire ecosystem,” said Ashish Pherwani, partner and media and entertainment leader at EY India.

The report's wish list includes better rights awareness among creators, clearer royalty payouts, simpler compliance for shops, venues, events and public spaces, a one-stop licensing window and set rate cards where practical. It also proposes an export promotion council dedicated to music, and calls for closer work between government and industry, more regulatory certainty and formal training in music creation and management. Vasant Sangeet Dwar, the country's first single-portal system for licensing public performances, went live in February 2026. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-variety-article-mid-articleX-uid2' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["btf","mid-articleX","mid"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-articleX") .addSize([[320,480],[300,250],[300,251],[620,366]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

“India possesses a unique opportunity to emerge as one of the world's leading music markets and cultural exporters. By nurturing talent across languages, regions, and genres, encouraging innovation while safeguarding creators' rights, and building stronger bridges between culture and commerce, we can unlock the full potential of India's music creator economy,” said Lily Pandeya, joint secretary at India's Ministry of Culture.

The findings arrive alongside CISAC's 2026 Global Collections Report, published in the organization's centenary year, which showed music creator royalties worldwide up 11.9%. Digital collections rose 27.9% and now make up 45.6% of the total, while live and background music became creators' second-biggest income source globally.

Youssou N'Dour, vice-president of CISAC (the International Confederation of Societies of Authors and Composers), said India's music scene mirrors a worldwide shift in which creators are reaching audiences at unprecedented scale. “The future of the industry will depend on ensuring that creators have the knowledge, rights and opportunities needed to build sustainable careers and continue enriching our societies through music,” he said.

For a sense of what an export push could deliver, the report points to South Korea, where K-pop generated more than $3 billion in overseas music-led revenue in 2025.

articles.title: Over 400 U.K. Industry Figures Demand End to “Culture of Open Secrets” After Russell Brand Trial
articles.summary: The open letter warns against calling Brand’s 10-and-a-half-year sentence a turning point: “It has taken some 17 years for justice.”
articles.content:
More than 400 U.K. entertainment industry professionals have signed an open letter, released Monday, calling on leaders at studios, broadcasters and unions to end the culture of silence and secrecy that the signatories say allowed Russell Brand 's abuse to go unchecked. Brand was sentenced last week to 10 and a half years in prison for rape and sexual assault.

The letter, billed as an "open letter to the creative industry, from the creative industry," comes as Little Britain star David Walliams faces allegations of sexual misconduct. A joint investigation by The Guardian and ITV News includes accounts from two women who say Walliams groomed them after meeting them when they were 15. Walliams denies wrongdoing. The letter asks those in power to "review your processes, protect those who speak out and become less offended by your inaction being named than you are by the actions you are being asked to recognize." blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-article-mid-article-uid0' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article1","mid-articleX","mid","mid-article"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article") .addSize([[300,250],[2,2],[300,251],[620,350],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4],[300,251]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; }); Related Stories General News Brit List 2026: Cornwall Outlaw Series, Coming-of-Age Film Top List of Unproduced Film, TV Scripts Movies Dual Oscar Winner Christopher Hampton Calls Glenn Close Honorary Oscar "the Least They Can Do," Says AI Is Just "a Super Google"

The letter was written by writer-actor-producer Ben Fletcher, co-organized by Alexa Morden and published on a dedicated website, makethisaturningpoint.com. Signatories include actors, directors and producers such as Natalie Dormer ( Game of Thrones , The Hunger Games ) and Richard Armitage ( The Hobbit ). The letter calls on the government to "act, not debate" by "increasing support for victims, ensuring police forces are fully resourced, and forcing accountability for those who know but choose convenient ignorance."

Brand's sentencing on Nov. 9, after a high-profile London trial in which he testified in his own defense, is a major catalyst for the letter. But the letter opens with a warning against calling this moment a turning point for a problem that has plagued the entertainment industry for decades. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-dsk-tab-mid-article2-uid1' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid","mid-article2","mid-articleX"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article2") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,350],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

"To afford such a label would be to ignore that it has taken some 17 years for justice," it reads. The letter adds that one witness in Brand's trial received death threats online, and that during the trial his lawyer threatened the reporter who uncovered his crimes.

On Monday, Brand released a statement through his wife , Laura Brand, who appeared to hold back tears as she read his claim of innocence in a video posted to YouTube. Britain's Justice Secretary Alex Norris called the broadcast of a statement from Brand while in prison "completely unacceptable."

"Prisoners are rightly banned from making statements that cause distress to victims," Norris wrote on X. "This is being urgently investigated, and I expect action to be taken if he is found to have broken the rules."

"For this to be a turning point, the creative and entertainment industries must first acknowledge the role they play in enabling the behaviour on trial and at the centre of these convictions," the letter reads. "Not through PR-drafted statements, vague promises or weak admissions that more could be done. But by accepting what was missed and that, collectively, the sector operates with a culture of open secrets and a belief that fame is a shield and status is a reason to look the other way.

"This cannot be dismissed as a one-off. Not when, this very week, allegations against another have been made public. Not when open secrets persist and the next documentary is already in pre-production. And the industry cannot mistake the lack of formal reporting for the absence of systemic abuse when many victims feel able to share their stories only quietly, too often prefixed with ‘I have nowhere else to go,' and the name of the union or organisation that failed them." blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-thr-article-mid-articleX-uid2' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["btf","mid-articleX","mid"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-articleX") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,350],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4]]) .setLazyLoadMultiplier(2) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

Fletcher writes that the fear of losing work or other opportunities is "a tool of control to shape narrative, maintain perceptions and discredit victims."

"And a person's credits and notoriety cannot and must not excuse their actions or attacks on those whose voices they believe beneath them," the letter states.

The signatories call on "every union, every company and every industry organisation" to stop allowing and perpetuating a "systemic cycle of abuse, whether through unconscious inaction or deliberate distraction."

articles.content:

articles.title: Avengers: Secret Wars Director Teases Marvel Film Will Make a Big Change From Other MCU Movies
articles.summary: As the clock ticks down for the Dec. 16 release date of Avengers: Doomsday, Marvel Studio's head honchos are already looking ahead to what comes next. Similar to the Thanos arc that culminated with Infinity War and Endgame, Doctor Doom's epic will also take place across two interconnected films, with the latter being Secret Wars […]
articles.content:
With a full month away before the film arrives in theaters, Doomsday is continuing to make headlines as more and more pieces are revealed. Its constantly growing roster of characters is already unparalleled compared to the last two Avengers , with a recent addition of a surprising X-Men character quietly announced last week. On top of that, Hugh Jackman let it slip that Wolverine and Deadpool should be showing up in the movie in one way or another, but like all of these characters, their role (and multiversal location) remain to be determined. With so much happening already, the sequel looks to up the scale to a whole other level.

In an interview with Empire , Marvel Studios President Kevin Feige promised that the upcoming Secret Wars “is a whole other genre of story” to Doomsday . Director Joe Russo added to that, stating that the Doomsday sequel will be “a really unique world” with a “unique story” that will be very different than what we are used to seeing. “The only reason to get out of bed every day is to take risks and surprise people and try things that have never been tried before. I think Secret Wars is one of those movies where I hope people will walk out of it and go, ‘I’ve never seen anything like that in my life!’”

This sounds like Hollywood hyperbole meant purely to sell tickets, but by all accounts — it's working. Without fully knowing what will happen in Doomsday , we can only take guesses based on events from the comic books that could flesh out what a potential movie could be like. If we're following the 1984 Battleworld arc by Jim Shooter, it's going to be a huge Royal Rumble of every hero and villain in the world colliding to see whether the forces of good or evil prevail. At the time when the original comics were published, it was a huge deal to see so many characters crossing over in the same place at the same time. However, we already got a world-encompassing crossover in Endgame , and it feels too soon to repeat the same tactic.

Jonathan Hickman's Secret Wars from 2015 might be the key to solving how it fits into Doomsday and why Feige and Russo feel it's going to be such a change of pace. I'll try not to spoil it too much for folks who would like to read this or wait to see the movie adaptation, but it involves Dr. Doom, multiverses and a whole lot of reality-shifting. It also helped merge a few characters from their Ultimate universe into the 616 world, which raises the question of whether Marvel characters from different studios could be wrapped up into this epic film or which ones we simply haven't seen yet could make their debut in an unexpected way . There's also the chance it revives a few other high-profile characters who haven't been seen in a while or who were killed off (such as Thanos) to give them a shot at redemption or perhaps something else we don't yet understand.

There are many rumors about the events Doomsday depicts, many of which are apocalyptic in nature (not the Oscar Isaac character) and would result in sweeping changes across the franchise. What isn't hyperbole to say is December's movie will be the catalyst of something big for the entire MCU in a way that hasn't happened yet, and if all goes according to Feige's plan, the landscape will truly be reshaped into something we have never seen before.

Do you think Secret Wars can pull off what Feige and Russo have suggested, or are they overhyping things more than they need to? Let us know in the comments below.

articles.title: Kevin Feige Reveals The 6 Words That Led to Robert Downey Jr. Returning to the MCU as Doctor Doom
articles.summary: Image Courtesy of Marvel Doctor Doom is coming to the MCU in Avengers: Doomsday, and it turns out that the discussion for this started with six words. It was Kevin Feige who got the ball rolling when he approached Robert Downey Jr.'s agent at a movie premiere and said six words to the man. Feige told him, "We have […]
articles.content:
The new issue of Empire Magazine has broken down the upcoming movie, and it includes the reveal of what Kevin Feige said to start Robert Downey Jr.'s return to the franchise as Doctor Doom . What is most surprising is that Feige said the six words at the premiere of Ant-Man and the Wasp: Quantumania .

Kevin Feige first approached Robert Downey Jr.’s agent at the ‘ANT-MAN AND THE WASP: QUANTUMANIA’ premiere about returning to the #MCU as Doctor Doom with a cryptic message: “We have an idea. It’s time.” (via @empiremagazine ) pic.twitter.com/PBeuwj5wkE

This is interesting timing. When Ant-Man and the Wasp: Quantumania was released, the next Avengers movie wasn't even going to be Avengers: Doomsday . The movie was going to be called Avengers: The Kang Dynasty . The main villain was going to be Kang, and this would lead into Avengers: Secret Wars . In fact, the post-credits scenes in Ant-Man and the Wasp: Quantumania showed the Council of Kangs, and then Kang was a big part of the Loki series on Disney+, setting up the entire idea for Avengers: The Kang Dynasty .

At the time of this discussion between Kevin Feige and Robert Downey Jr.'s agent, Ant-Man and the Wasp: Quantumania hadn't flopped yet. Furthermore, Jonathan Majors was still signed on to play Kang. It seemed like it wasn't until Marvel fired Majors that the movie idea changed to Avengers: Doomsday . In the end, it made sense because it was Doctor Doom who was the man responsible for creating Battleworld in “Secret Wars” in the comics, so he should be the one who did it in the MCU.

However, it also makes sense when you step back and look at the situation. Just because the first movie was Avengers: The Kang Dynasty , it didn't mean that Doctor Doom wasn't showing up as well to create Battleworld. It would be easy to see Kang causing all the problems with the incursions thanks to a new multiversal war breaking out between Kangs. Then, just when Kang was about to destroy everything, Doctor Doom could have stepped in to save the day and create the story for Avengers: Secret Wars . Majors being fired could have just forced Marvel to bring in Doom sooner. Doom was likely planned all along, and it seems that the Ant-Man and the Wasp: Quantumania premiere was when these discussions started.

articles.title: 5 Dead Superheroes Who Took Forever to Come Back to Life
articles.summary: Image Courtesy of DC Comics In both Marvel and DC Comics, death is frequently treated as just a mere inconvenience. Whenever a superhero dies, they often only have to wait a few months or a couple of years before popping right out of the grave to continue crimefighting. Fan reactions to these resurrections have ranged from excitement to anger. Yet […]
articles.content:
Superhero deaths are always more impactful when they’re given time to rest, and their loved ones have time to grieve and move on. And when these long dead heroes finally return, they find the world has changed in ways they never could have imagined.

1985’s Crisis on Infinite Earths was one of the most monumental events in comic book history , and saw many iconic heroes and villains lose their lives. One of the most stunning deaths of the series was that of Kara Zor-El, aka Supergirl. In Crisis on Infinite Earths #7 , Superman’s cousin tried to destroy the Anti-Monitor to end his multiversal genocide. Unfortunately, the Anti-Monitor gained the upper hand and killed Supergirl. After the Crisis on Infinite Earths , the DC Universe was rebooted, and several new Supergirls were introduced to replace Kara. Instead of Kryptonians, the new Supergirls included a shapeshifting alien robot called Matrix and the human Linda Danvers. Eventually, the original Supergirl would make her climactic return in 2004’s Superman/Batman #8 19 years after she died. Rather than a straightforward resurrection, Kara’s return was DC Comics rebooting her character and origin for the post-Crisis timeline. Since then, Supergirl has once again cemented herself as one of the most important members of Superman’s family.

Along with Supergirl, another significant hero killed during the Crisis on Infinite Earths was the second Flash, Barry Allen. In 1985’s Crisis on Infinite Earths #8 , Barry ran as fast as he could to tear apart the Anti-Monitor’s antimatter cannon so it wouldn’t destroy the five remaining universes. While the plan worked, Barry pushed himself too far, disintegrating into dust and becoming one with the Speed Force. Afterward, Barry’s mantle would be picked up by his sidekick, Wally West , the former Kid Flash. Wally would then be the primary Flash in DC Comics for decades. It would take 23 years for Barry to return officially in 2008’s Final Crisis #2 . In the issue, Barry managed to break himself free of the Speed Force and return to the world of the living after narrowly escaping the Black Racer. Since then, Barry and Wally have taken turns operating as the main Flash of DC Comics.

The Doom Patrol is one of the most underrated superhero teams in DC Comics history. But, in 1968 all its members met a tragic end. Doom Patrol #121 was the final issue of the original series, and with it, the core four members of the Doom Patrol, Robot Man, Elasti-Girl, Negative Man, and the Chief, sacrificed their lives to save a city from being destroyed by a bomb. And while most of the Doom Patrol were eventually revealed to have cheated death, Elasti-Girl was the only one who stayed buried. The shapeshifting hero remained dead for 36 years until the events of 2006’s Infinite Crisis , when Superboy-Prime rewrote all of existence with a reality punch. This event changed Elasti-Girl’s history, so the Chief salvaged a piece of her skull and used it to regrow her body. Although she was initially under the Chief’s control, Elasti-Girl eventually broke free. Now, Elasti-Girl has reestablished herself as a core member of the Doom Patrol.

Few comic book characters have made a more iconic return after their supposed death than Bucky Barnes. Captain America's plucky sidekick, Bucky was presumed dead after Avengers # 4 in 1964. During World War II, the heroic duo tried to stop Baron Zemo’s drone from attacking the Allied Forces. However, the drone was booby-trapped and blew up. The explosion led to Captain America freezing in ice for decades and to Bucky presumably being c killed in action. Bucky’s death became an integral part of Captain America’s character as he was haunted by his inability to save his friend. Yet, in 2005’s Captain America Vol. 5 #6 , Bucky’s death was retconned so that he not only survived but was transformed into the brainwashed Russian assassin, the Winter Soldier. Having been considered dead for 41 years, Bucky’s return was a huge surprise that forever changed Captain America’s lore. Additionally, Bucky has since broken free of his brainwashing and become a hero once again.

The X-Men have suffered many losses over the years, but few deaths were once thought to be more permanent than Thunderbird's. Debuting as a member of the All-New All-Different X-Men, Thunderbird only lasted three issues before he tragically died in 1975’s X-Men # 95 . In the issue, the X-Men battled the villain Count Nefaria. When he tried to escape in a jet, Thunderbird’s stubbornness led him to jump onto the jet and tear it apart until it exploded, killing him. Since then, Thunderbird only made brief appearances as an undead soldier or a spirit. However, that would all change 46 years later in 2021’s The Trail of Magneto #5. At this time, the mutant nation of Krakoa assembled the Five, a group of mutants who discovered the key to resurrection. Working together, the Five resurrected almost every mutant who had ever died, including Thunderbird. After being brought back to life, Thunderbird would dedicate himself to protecting the Apache people and mutantkind.

Which superhero were you most excited to see make their comeback? Leave a Comment below and join the conversation in the ComicBook Forum!

articles.title: 5 Dark Fantasy Anime to Watch on Crunchyroll in November 2026
articles.summary: Image Courtesy of Crunchyroll The ever-growing popularity of the anime industry has many enthusiasts looking to venture into the world of exciting shows and movies. No doubt, as the world's largest streaming platform for anime fans, Crunchyroll is the one platform fans would go to in order to browse new series. However, the platform is full of over a thousand anime […]
articles.content:
The Fall 2026 anime season kicked off last month, and all major platforms, especially Crunchyroll, have released exciting new shows for fans across the globe. Crunchyroll by far had the biggest anime lineup for the season, just like every other quarter, with new weekly releases to keep fans busy for the rest of the year. However, since the latest season’s anime was released only released last month, there aren’t enough episodes for fans to binge. If you’re looking for new anime shows to watch this month that have already released full seasons, then this list is perfect for you.

Not only is it one of the most famous anime exclusively available on Crunchyroll, but it is also one of the highest-rated isekai of all time. The anime series is based on the acclaimed light novel written by Tappei Nagatsuki and illustrated by Shinichiro Ootsuka. Two years after the novel debuted in 2016, the White Fox animation studio released the anime adaptation, which continues to return with new sequels. 2026 marks the 10th anniversary of the anime, and over all these years, four seasons have been released, as the story keeps getting more intense.

The anime is often praised for exciting plot twists, unique worldbuilding, and thrilling action as it centers around Subaru Natsuki, an ordinary teenage boy. After leaving a convenience store one evening, he suddenly finds himself transported into another world. Equipped with the ability to return to time, Subaru tries his best to adjust to the new world while also dealing with any threat that comes his way.

This dark fantasy from MAPPA is based on an older manga which was serialized from 2000 to 2018. The anime shares strong aesthetic ties with gritty details while following a hyper-violent Japanese animation that’s reminiscent of the 1990s. The story takes place in an underground alley called the Hole, which draws heavily from the grimy, pipe-filled, rain-slicked urban dystopias seen in 90s cyberpunk and Seinen anime such as Ghost in the Shell: Memories or Battle Angel Alita . The animation style uses 2D and 3D CG by the studio, but the design philosophy and aesthetics aren’t that different from the cult spirit of the 1990s animation.

The anime debuted in 2000, and it took MAPPA six years to return with a second season this year. A third season has already been confirmed , and fans are awaiting updates on the anime as Caiman and Nikaido get closer to discovering the dark secrets lingering in the alleys of the Hole while also uncovering what transpired in the past.

Puella Magi Madoka Magica is an acclaimed fantasy classic on Crunchyroll with a surprise dark twist beneath its cheerful facade. The story focuses on magical girls and remains one of the most shocking series of all time. The award-winning show released its anime adaptation in 2011 before returning with sequel films in 2012 and 2013. This acclaimed original series follows Madoka Kaname and Sayaka Miki, two middle school girls whose ordinary lives take drastic turns after encountering Kyuubey, a mysterious magical familiar. Kyuubey offers the girls an offer to grant any one of their wishes if they become magical girls.

The girls can gain enough power to fulfill their dreams. However, Homura Akemi, a new transfer student and a magical girl, tries her best to stop them from accepting the offer. She claims that the offer isn’t what it looks like, implying there will be a major price to pay.

However, among the major titles of the season, a new action fantasy series quickly climbed the ranks. Sentenced to Be a Hero caused huge waves in the anime industry after its debut on Crunchyroll as it captured fans’attention with its spectacular animation, unique premise, and promising plot. The anime is not only highly rated but also offers a lot of unique concepts, which make it stand out from the rest. The anime series is based on a light novel written by Rocket Shoukai and illustrated by Mephisto.

This dark fantasy story offers a twisted outlook on the role of a hero since this title is given only to those who have committed the most heinous crimes. While almost all fantasy stories glorify the coveted title of hero, this anime considers it the worst punishment anyone can ever receive. Heroes are those who serve in the military in an endless war against the Demon Lords. However, the worst part is that the convicts aren’t even allowed to die. If they somehow lose their lives in the battle, they will be resurrected over and over again, so they will keep fighting a never-ending war. The resurrection process is brutal since it forces the soul of a hero straight out of hell and puts it back into its corpse.

When it comes to modern anime, specifically those released in the 2010s and 2020s, Attack on Titan ‘s legacy can’t be matched with anything else. Written and illustrated by Hajime Isayama, the manga reached its controversial finale in 2021, which sparked so much fury from fans that the creator was losing sleep over it. Attack on Titan follows Eren Yeager, a boy whose mother is devoured by a Titan when monstrous, humanoid beings breach his hometown’s walls.

This trauma ignites a burning obsession to destroy every Titan. What starts as a survival horror story quickly transforms into political intrigue. From Eren’s ability to transform into a Titan, the origins of Titans, the truth about the attack on Shiganshina during Eren’s childhood, the world outside of Eldia, and, of course, Eren’s true goal, Attack on Titan has been a wild ride at every turn of the story. It’s one of those stories that keeps fans engaged with these twists, as every plot point and foreshadowing starts to make sense after the truth is revealed. However, once things are set in motion, there’s no way of changing what has been done. Is there any series or movie you like that didn’t make it to the list? articles.title: Robert Pattinson's James Bond Will Make Movie History By Changing 1 Word From the Rest of the Franchise
articles.summary: White smoke has emerged from MGM as a new James Bond has officially been revealed, with Robert Pattinson taking on the iconic role. The times are a-changing, though, because in years past the christening of a new 007 would have been a major event. Thanks to the character's cultural status in the UK, massive press […]
articles.content:
Not only will Pattinson be taking on the part and bringing a new performance to the character after his announcement was distinct, but the team behind the scenes is different too. After ousting Barbara Broccoli and Michael G. Wilson, Amazon MGM has put Amy Pascal and David Heyman behind the series as its producers . Perhaps the biggest change that James Bond 26 will make is a subtle one, though; it's just a one-word change that will be different from every other movie in the entire film franchise, and it's all about who James Bond is working for: The King.

Queen Elizabeth II began her reign as the monarch of the UK on February 6, 1952, just one year before the publication of the first James Bond novel, Casino Royale , and ten years prior to the first James Bond movie, Dr. No . That means that for the entirety of James Bond's life as a fictional character in books and feature films, his career as a secret agent working for MI6 has been described with five words. These five words even became the title of one of the books and one of the best movies in the series: “ On Her Majesty's Secret Service .”

On September 8, 2022, eleven months after the release of Daniel Craig's final James Bond movie, No Time to Die , Queen Elizabeth II passed away and was succeeded by her son, making him King Charles III. As a result, when Robert Pattinson's James Bond makes his debut, he'll not only be the first Bond from a new creative regime, but he'll be the first ever to work “On His Majesty's Secret Service.” This one-word change may not seem like a big deal in the slightest to some, but the fact that the change has been made at all speaks to not only the length of Elizabeth's reign but how much it has defined things, even pop culture like James Bond's career.

It's worth noting that Robert Pattinson's James Bond will be the first movie in the series to acknowledge this change to UK politics, but it's technically not the first Bond story to do so. Earlier this year, the 007: First Light video game that arrived to critical acclaim back in May did the same thing. All that in mind, though, Pattinson being referred to with a job title that no other big-screen Bond has been given will immediately differentiate him from what's come before. Beyond that subtle change, it remains to be seen how different the new film will be from what has come before it, but small details beget even bigger changes, and we could be in store for something distinct with the new Bond.

Victoria Pedretti is reportedly in the running for the role of MYSTIQUE in the MCU, and she is apparently Marvel Studios’ top choice for the role! 📰: @JamesMackwl pic.twitter.com/81YsGLgFUI

Victoria Pedretti had her breakout role on The Haunting of Hill House , the Mike Flanagan miniseries based on the Shirley Jackson novel. She played Nell on the series, and she quickly made her name in the horror genre. She played Love Quinn in the thriller series You , and then she took on the main role of Dani in the next Flanagan miniseries, The Haunting of Bly Manor . She debuted on the big screen with a supporting role in Quentin Tarantino's Once Upon a Time in Hollywood . Now, she could have a chance at the biggest movie role of her career.

Pedretti is 31, and even though she is only six years older than Inde Navarrette , the MCU probably won't need to change the relationship between her and Rogue. Rogue and Mystique both appeared in the original X-Men trilogy, and their relationship was never in play, so it might not happen in the MCU either.

Adding her to the MCU could really help the X-Men's impressive cast get even better.

articles.title: Attack on Titan Doesn't Need a Comeback After Its Perfect Ending
articles.summary: Image Courtesy of MAPPA Despite fan backlash during the manga's serialization, it's pretty obvious at this point that Attack on Titan already has a perfect ending. When it comes to anime series released in the 2010s and 2020s, their legacy can't be matched by anything else. In fact, the controversy at the time was so intense that Hajime Isayama, […]
articles.content:
Established in 2011, MAPPA is known as one of the most renowned animation studios in Japan. While its popularity skyrocketed in the 2020s with the release of Jujutsu Kaisen and a few other acclaimed shows, the studio had a strong foundation with exceptional shows and movies under its belt ever since its establishment. Fans naturally had high expectations from the studio for the final season, especially since the time-skip changed the entire narrative. MAPPA not only lived up to the expectations, but delivered the best possible version of the story in the final season and special episodes. The anime reached its conclusion on November 4th, 2023, with the release of the second special episode of Attack on Titan: Final Season – The Final Chapters .

The final stretch of the manga sparked numerous controversies with nuanced scenes that not many appreciated, as well as the death of beloved characters. The ending became less hated despite having reasonable detractors after the anime adaptation , since a few years had passed by then, and the original scenes soothed fans’ disappointment. The problem with cynical or analytical endings is that not everyone will perceive them in the same way. Additionally, Mikasa kissing Eren’s severed head should’ve been an emotional moment of the story, but it didn’t have the impact it should’ve because of its off-putting execution.

The cycle never truly ended in the series, leaving room for a sequel or a spin-off, but the creator has yet to return with a new story. Several decades after Eren’s death, Paradis is still destroyed, and a young boy with a dog discovers the tree where Eren was buried, which now has the same appearance as the tree where Ymir gained the power of the Titans. The implication is that the boy may gain the abilities of a Titan, thereby bringing that destructive power into the world again. Hence, there’s a strong possibility that the current world remains at risk of going through everything all over again, implying that peace is not everlasting.

Considering how much fans hated the finale when the manga was being serialized, not many expected that the controversy would completely die down after the anime adaptation. Isayama was also involved in the production and worked closely with the anime staff to refine dialogue and certain moments while subtly adding original scenes. He also helped tweak many scenes to make the emotional beats land more sincerely than they did in the manga. The anime didn’t make major changes from the original, but these minor details and the presentation with stunning animation made a world of difference.

This not only made fans forget their initial dissatisfaction with the manga, but also helped the series reach new heights of global popularity. The anime was well-received thanks to all the efforts of the studio and the creator. Despite taking the torch from WIT Studio during a controversial moment and the tight deadlines, MAPPA’s adaptation saved the series with one of the best adaptations in recent years. Since Isayama didn’t work on any extra chapter or spin-off, there won’t be another anime episode or movie with a completely new story.

However, that doesn’t mean the end of the franchise since both WIT Studio and MAPPA keep returning with new projects and merchandise to keep fans intrigued.Its final chapters drive home its powerful — albeit bleak — message about the cycle of violence and human nature. And it gives the series and its characters an epic send-off from the beginning of Season 4. There’s tons of well-animated action, along with great callbacks to prior chapters and incredible character growth. It’s everything you could want in a finale, and it doesn’t deserve all the hate it gets.

Do you think MAPPA delivered the perfect ending for Attack on Titan ? What moment from the finale made the biggest impression on you? Share your thoughts in the comments below!

articles.title: 'The Fantasticks' Review: A Welcome Broadway Debut Seven Decades In The Making
articles.summary: Two trunks for storing theatrical props share the stage early in the new production of The Fantasticks, opening for the first time ever on Broadway tonight. One is "Hayes Theater" and the other "Sullivan Street Playhouse," as clear a mission statement as any fan of this stalwart of '60s whimsy could want. With a new […]
articles.content:
Two trunks for storing theatrical props share the stage early in the new production of The Fantasticks , opening for the first time ever on Broadway tonight. One is “Hayes Theater” and the other “Sullivan Street Playhouse,” as clear a mission statement as any fan of this stalwart of '60s whimsy could want.

With a new approach that reimagines the musical's star-crossed boy-meets-girl plot for a boy-meets-boy world, this revival directed by Christopher Gattelli arrives in the 21st Century with both a fresh attitude and a devotion to the spirit of a work that all but defined Off Broadway charm nearly 70 years ago. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-dsk-tab-mid-article1-uid0' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article1","mid","mid-articleX","mid-article","300x251"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article") .addSize([[2,2],[300,250],[620,350],[300,251],[501,282],[3,3],[2,4],[4,2],[620,366]]) .exemptFromSleep() .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; }); Related Stories News Bryan Cranston & Marianne Jean-Baptiste Heading To Broadway In Ivo Van Hove's Acclaimed 'All My Sons' Revival News 'Downstate' Broadway Review: Provocative Play About Sex Offenders Questions The Nature Of Forgiveness

Granted, that's a charm that might well be lost on some audiences today, much the way Pippin and Godspell could seem impossibly twee in a Broadway where Downstate just opened and a dance club take on Shakespeare has New Yorkers lining up outside the Winter Garden. Then again, this is also a Broadway where the very sweet Two Strangers (Carry A Cake Across New York ) held on longer than anyone imagined . Watch on Deadline if ( !window.pmc.harmony?.isEventAdScheduledTime() ) { pmcCnx.cmd.push(function() { pmcCnx({ settings: { plugins: { pmcAtlasMG: { iabPlcmt: 2, } } }, playerId: '32fe25c4-79aa-406a-af44-69b41e969e71', playlistId: '0199e506-e642-7728-8264-463efe71337b', }).render("connatix_contextual_player_div"); }); } else { // This should only be get called when page cache is not cleared and it's event time. window.pmc.harmony?.switchToHarmonyPlayer(); }

Gattelli and his fine cast of newcomers and veterans know perfectly well what they're up to – and up against, staying faithful to the winsomeness that kept The Fantasticks running Off Broadway for a total 42 years (!). They know that abandoning the ingratiating amiability and theater-kid appeal of this Tom Jones-Harvey Schmidt musical that gave early breaks to Jerry Orbach and many generations of soon-to-be stars would be like cutting “Try To Remember” from the score.

No small part of this revival's pleasures are the coming together of relative newcomers – Maxim Chlumecky and Nathan Levy as the two boys, Fire Island ‘s Zane Phillips making an impressive Broadway debut as El Gallo – with beloved stage figures Leslie Rodriguez Kritzer and Ruthie Ann Miles (as the mothers). They're all terrific singers with crowd-pleasing comic skills – Kritzer and Miles perform a splendid song-and-dance number, “Never Say No,” early in the show – and their matched by a supporting cast that includes David Patrick Kelly, Kevin del Aguila and Ahmad Simmons. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-dl-mid-article-inject2-uid1' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article2","mid-articleX","mid-article","mid","300x251"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article2") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,350],[2,4],[4,2],[620,366]]) .exemptFromSleep() .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

The musical's lovely score, including the stand-out “Try To Remember” as well as once-familiar songs like “Much More,” “Soon It's Gonna Rain” and “I Can See It” that crossed over to wider audiences when Barbra Streisand and others covered them back when the stage was a routine conduit to pop charts, retains its appeal (even if purists might sniff at Sam Davis' appealing new orchestrations that add strings, woodwinds and some brass to the famously minimalist piano and harp sound of the original production and its 1960 cast album.

So, the plot – and keep in mind it falls somewhere between allegory and fairy tale, with a touch of the foolery and disguised motivations of Shakespearean comedy tossed in, and never quite matching its intended heights much less its sources. The two youths – Matt and Luisa in the original, Matt and Lewis here – are nextdoor neighbors, in love and pining but secretly, lest their feuding parents – fathers in the original, mothers here – demand a cease and desist.

Unbeknownst to the boys, the parents are actually great friends, and merely invented the fake feud to push the sons together. As the moms sing in the ode to reverse psychology “Never Say No,” “Dog's got to bark, a mule's got to bray/Soldiers must fight and preachers must pray/And children, I guess, must get their own way/The minute that you say no.”

The parents further conspire to recruit the famous magician, El Gallo, and two itinerant actors to fake-abduct Lewis so that Matt can play the hero and seal the lovers' happy ending. All goes as planned, until the moonlit bliss of Act I gives way to the buyer's remorse of Act II. The boys long for freedom – from one another – and the mothers descend to bickering and frayed nerves.

Another happy ending, older and wiser, eventually arrives, and here, as always, the musical's increasingly cloying second act drags and strains under its own contrivances. Gattelli, with the same know-how he brought to Schmigadoon! and Death Becomes Her , goes quite a way in almost making us overlook the musical's weaknesses, and he's helped by his really game cast (Chlumecky, as Matt, the more boyishly adventuresome of the boys, steals just about every scene he's in).

Gattelli's restrained choreography, including some full-on dance numbers but just as often simpler movement and joyful bounding, works well with the minimalist traditions of the show, which extend to Jason Sherwood's set design (the usual brick theater backdrop, a cut-out crescent moon, wheeled-in window frames now and then, a sweet flowering of greenery and starlight at the right moment) and Linda Cho's costumes that blend the boys' normcore with the showily sexy bandit flash of El Gallo.

As is this show's custom, the wall that's erected by the parents to keep the kids faux-apart is played by a silent actor (Ahmad Simmons, in concrete-gray formalwear and stovepipe hat) who stands between the two households (each side represented by a small plot of vegetation, flowers on one side, veggies on the other).

In this production, that character retains the traditional billing as “The Mute,” a dated term that here survives, unlike the original's use of the word “rape” that, even in 1960, was an archaic synonym for “abduction” (as in Alexander Pope's 1712 poem “The Rape of the Lock”). Here, as in most productions of the musical, they make the wise decision to just say abduction. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-dsk-tab-mid-articleX-uid2' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-articleX","mid-article","btf","300x251"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-articleX") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,366]]) .exemptFromSleep() ; });

Even without doing a word-for-word comparison of the original Tom Jones (no, not that Tom Jones) lyrics and the ones he revised for this version shortly before his death in 2023 , the musical supports the gender-switch with remarkable ease. Levy portrays Lewis (née Luisa) with a disarming celebration of guilelessness and an ingénue's “I feel pretty” self-infatuation. The casting is on-point, with the small-framed and black-haired Levy to a nice visual counterpoint to Chlumecky's more athletic build and blond halo of curls. They, and everything else in this production, work together to bring a theatrical warhorse galloping into 21st Century Broadway, surprising us with just how much pluck it can still carry.

However, the best news is that the new character will be played by Matthew Lillard, who is in the middle of a career resurgence. Deadline reported Lillard's addition to the Anything But Ghosts cast, but there is no word on who he is playing or what his role will be in the movie.

Curry Barker didn't have many people looking over his shoulder when he was making Obsession , but it looks like he might be running into a little trouble with his follow-up Anything But Ghosts . Barker is not only directing the movie, but he is starring in it alongside his co-screenwriter, Cooper Tomlinson. Barker and Tomlinson play two con-artist ghost hunters who rig up scenes to rip off grieving clients. However, when they land a job that involves actual ghosts, they find themselves in over their heads.

While this sounds like the cult classic Peter Jackson movie The Frighteners , Barker makes it seem like it will be much darker. Tomlinson described it as what would happen if Key and Peele walked into Hereditary , making it sound like it might have the dark humor of The Frighteners , but it will be a lot more of a horror movie than that one ever was. The other thing to note is that it takes place in the same universe as Obsession , and no less than Seth Rogen said the movie is better than Obsession .

Barker had a test screening a month ago, and it was said to go well, but Barker has gone into reshoots anyway. The fact that he has added Matthew Lillard in a mystery role means this is more than just fixing some scenes. With a new character, Barker is adding new material to the original movie's cut. This is big news for Lillard fans, as he continues to have a huge career resurgence. Most recently, he has starred in the Five Nights at Freddy's movie franchise, returned to the latest Scream movie, and even took on a major role in Mike Flanagan's Carrie miniseries . Next year, he has a role in James Gunn's Man of Tomorrow , and earlier this year, he had a role in Daredevil: Born Again Season 2.
